newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Analysts expect better 2nd half for CHH.
newsitem.headline: Analysts expect better 2nd half for CHH.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd looked to be over the worst of the pulp and paper cycle in the first half and should look forward to an improvement in the second, forest sector analysts said on Thursday.

CHH earlier reported a decline in net profit to NZ$118 million in the six months to September from $271 million a year earlier, adding it was confident the improvement seen in the second quarter would continue in the second half.
"I think the second half will certainly be better than the first," David Stanley at Doyle Paterson Brown said.
Analysts said the result was in line with expectations, but the company's operating performance was a little better than anticipated.
Stanley said this was the case particularly in pulp and paper, where the company benefited from higher margins.
"That came about through higher prices and better operating efficiencies and clearly the involvement of the tissues business, where they got better margins," he said.
Analysts said the first quarter appeared to have spanned the worst of the pulp and paper cycle. Second quarter earnings rose to NZ$62 million from $56 million in the first.
The share market took the result in its stride and by 11.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) the stock was up one cent at NZ$3.23.
While the company appeared to still be in a cyclically difficult time, Chief Executive John Faraci was quietly confident the worst was over.
Since the start of the financial year, the price of softwood pulp and risen to US$550 from $500 per tonne and Faraci was optimistic improved trading conditions would continue.
Analysts were encouraged by progress on cost savings, where the company intended to shave NZ$25 million in the current year, rising to $50 million in 1997/8.
But there was still uncertainty in the industry and a risk that pulp and paper prices could still drop.

"It's really in the hands of the northern hemisphere pulp producers as to what happens there," Doyle Paterson's Stanley said. "If they restrain production then the market should tighten going into 1997," he said.
"Despite that, the second half -- under most scenarios -- is going to be better because wood products are looking better."
Analysts are now looking at a full year result in the late NZ$200 millions.
Francis Loo at SBC Warburg said the decision to attach dividend withholding credits for non-resident shareholders was a positive one, allowing a higher effective yield for foreign investors.
While opinions still varied on the commodities outlook, SBC belonged to the "slow recovery scenario" but Loo said there may yet be renewed weakness in pulp.
However, the overall picture of the company was one where its three main businesses were at the bottom of their cycles rather than the top.

"So we would be definitely see a stronger second half relative to the first half result. The only question will be the quantum of pickup and I guess that's the question that is on everybody's mind at the moment," she said.
Loo said a full year result of NZ$250 to $270 million now looked achievable for CHH, which is 50.3 percent owned by International Paper.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
